pages.text: In the past it was believed the world we live on is a sphere-like object in a large space orbiting around similar planets. We simply cannot perceive its curvature because of its absolute size. Things like the Nether are simply another layer in the crust of the planet, situated beneath the unbreakable bedrock layer, whereas the End is present somewhere in the vast space outside of this world.

Yet now, after some people have broken through the bedrock by unorthodox means, we know this idea to be false. In reality, this existence seems to be comprised of various 'planes' or 'layers' such as this main world, which is usually called the 'Overworld', separated by borders of bedrock and sky/void. These planes exist in a sort of void, where a person cannot normally cross from one into another, with the exception of when these planes 'collide'. Such examples are

portals that can connect them. There have also been cases where 'falling' from one world can result in appearing in a different one. Still, it might be better to assume that these planes do not exist on each other like layers of soil, and instead either take up the same space at different instances of existence or are present in a chaotic space where the connection between two points is not necessarily a line. Either way, if this is truly how these multitudes of worlds work, it brings into

question their origin. It's clear that outside of the Overworld, all others planes embody some sort of essences. The Nether is filled with flame and undeath. The End is ruled by space and 'alien-ness' - for a lack of a better word. Meanwhile, some embody the mystical twilight itself, while others can be as mundane as bees. With all these taken into consideration, two conflicting conclusions come to mind: First is that the Overworld is the center of existence where all the essences from various

planes converge - in varying densities - and form a sort of balance. The second, which seems more probable to me, is that the Overworld is the original world from which all other planes were broken off and devolved into their primordial form. Either conclusion, however, would require either a higher authority which enabled the balance of such a fragmented existence or an event that could have caused the 'rupture' of a main, unified world and the present situation is
a naturally developed balance after considerably time passed.
